cohort: 302 high-risk pregnant women (233 Turkish citizens and 69 Syrian refugees)
finding: Despite differences in some maternal characteristics, pregnancy and neonatal outcomes were similar between Turkish citizens and Syrian refugees with high-risk pregnancies.
mod_finding: This study found that rates of cesarean section were significantly higher in Turkish citizens compared to Syrian refugees, but rates of live birth, preterm birth, and low birth weight were not significantly different between the two groups.
